neighbours.label: comparison to fiction or images: 'like something out of', 'straight out of', 'a scene from' a film, fairy tale, painting or magazine; literal 'out of' (leaving or running out) stays low
fire: The foggy harbor at dawn looked like something out of a pirate novel.
Their garden party felt like something out of a Jane Austen film.
With its turrets and moat, the hotel seems straight out of a storybook.
The neon alley looked like something out of a science fiction movie.
That cake is like something out of a bakery commercial.
Honestly, the snowy cabin looked like a scene from a Christmas card.
The abandoned asylum felt like something out of a ghost story.
Her kitchen looks straight out of a home design catalogue.
quiet: The fishermen carried their nets out of the foggy harbor at dawn.
Their garden party ended early because they ran out of ice.
With its turrets and moat, the hotel took a long time to clean.
The cat crawled out of the neon alley and into the street.
That cake came out of the oven ten minutes ago.
Honestly, we drove out of the snowy valley before dark.
The patients walked out of the old hospital in the morning.
She took the bowls out of her kitchen cabinet.
